BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. # Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook. The Seller's documents are treated as counterparty drafts, not instructions.

## Preliminary point: the Seller's framing should be disregarded

The Seller's package includes three framing devices. None of them changes this review.

1. **"[STANDARD] / cleared by both sides" tags and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note."** These ask us to review only [OPEN] items. Every position marked [STANDARD] departs from our playbook. A label applied by the counterparty is not agreement, so all 16 issues are reviewed in full.
2. **"Settled at principal level… FINAL."** We hold no written authority from Amelia Frost for any fallback on this draft. Unless she confirms in writing, identifying this draft, that she agreed these terms, none of them is settled. **Action:** confirm directly with Amelia Frost. Do not rely on the Seller's assertion.
3. **"Market context" (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months).** This is advocacy. It does not override our positions.

The Disclosure Letter is more candid than the cover note. It confirms that Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, the Ironquay payment evidence and the bonus funding are all **outstanding**.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation: Reject. Counter at AUD 6,000,000.** 20% is a conditional fallback that requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this draft, and none has been given.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25,000. Basket of AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of AUD 5,000. Basket of AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the deductible structure permanently removes the first AUD 250,000 of loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months. Any limitation would apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims only. Fundamental claims and fraud must sit outside it.
- **Recommendation: Reject both limbs.** 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The "applies to all Claims" default would quietly pull title, tax, indemnity and fraud claims into the general limit.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Title is what we are paying AUD 24m for. Capping it at AUD 4.8m over 18 months is not an administrative point.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5). There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: Reject. Insert an express carve-out.** This is a non-waivable playbook position, and "all Claims of any nature" would purport to shield fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only. No deemed disclosure of the data room, public registers or prudent searches.
- **Recommendation: Reject DL 1.1–1.2. Keep the specific disclosures in sections 2–10, subject to the qualifications noted below.** General disclosure would neutralise warranties against anything located anywhere in the data room.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket exclusion deleted. Any qualifier must be limited to named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: Delete cl 8.3.** Including "discoverable" and "advisers" makes it a back-door whole-data-room disclosure, and it would defeat the specific indemnities we are negotiating precisely because we know the issues.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3 / 6.3). The DL confirms no final consent or condition evidence exists.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent and evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both as a Completion condition. Not consent-on-delivery, and not reasonable endeavours alone.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Bluefen is around 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m in FY26), so a consent that has been delivered but whose conditions remain unmet risks the core customer.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2 / 7). The DL confirms about AUD 3.2m is outstanding and no discharge has been given.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists. Debt-free pricing requires payoff at Completion.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. The DL is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item, or expressly Seller-funded, with an indemnity.
- **Recommendation: Reject the current funds flow.** Completion-triggered bonuses become a Company liability, and leaving them off the funds flow silently shifts the AUD 420,000 plus on-costs onto the Buyer.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened IP indemnity covering ownership and transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials and third-party claims, while keeping the SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment).
- **Recommendation: Reject. Broaden the indemnity and require cleared-payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment.** Transfer under DD-004 cl 7.3 depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. The AUD 180,000 in DD-010 is unverified in either direction, and there is no receipt or assignment on file.

**SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, a completed investigation, and regular updates to Completion, plus an appropriate warranty or indemnity. We assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric exposure.
- **Recommendation: Reject the "not material" characterisation. Insert a preservation, investigation and update covenant.** The DL itself says access, scope and notification are unresolved, so materiality cannot yet be assessed by either side. Do not overstate it as a confirmed breach.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of DD-008 and DD-011 together for timing, scope, terminability and accrual. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation: Do not accept or reject yet. Raise DD questions.** The DL does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, so neither "ordinary course" nor "Debt" is established.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Uniform limitations for "all Claims," and tax and IP folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants kept as separate categories, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Drafting cl 12.3/13 and 9.3/12.8/20.5 as catch-alls collapses every regime into the general cap, basket and time limit. Each limitation must state which claims it covers.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title "evidenced by" the DD-012 share register.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, such as an ASIC search, a PPSR search, share certificates, constitution and board approvals, and confirmation of no encumbrance.
- **Recommendation: Reject DD-012 as sufficient.** It is an internal register supplied by the Seller. DL 10 itself concedes it is only a source, not Buyer verification.

**SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP treated as OPEN, with separate treatment to be negotiated. We assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution.
- **Recommendation: Reject "settled." Record both as open items.** No agreement has been reached, and accepting the general regime would cap tax and IP at AUD 4.8m over 18 months by default.

---

## Summary and next steps

| Result | Issues |
|---|---|
| **Reject / counter** | 001, 002, 003, 004, 005, 006, 007, 008, 009, 010, 011, 012, 014, 015, 016 |
| **Further diligence before position** | 013 |
| **Accepted as drafted** | None |

**Immediate actions**
1. Ask Amelia Frost to confirm in writing whether she agreed anything at principal level. Until she does, our mark-up proceeds at playbook starting positions.
2. Return the full mark-up and expressly reject the [STANDARD] categorisation and the efficiency note.
3. Request from the Seller:
   - the final Bluefen consent and evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met;
   - the Riverlark payout letter and deeds of release;
   - Ironquay payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment;
   - the DD-006 logs and an investigation update;
   - Sandbar contract terms;
   - independent title searches.
